Details.RequiredDocuments: You are required to provide documentation that supports the eligibility and qualification claims made in your resume and assessment questionnaire. You must submit the applicable documents listed here and those listed with the eligibilities you select in the announcement questionnaire with your application package. Applicants who do not provide supporting documentation that fully support their claims will not be referred to the hiring manager. Cover letter is optional. A complete resume is required. Your resume must show relevant experience, job title, duties and accomplishments. Your resume must show complete information for each job entry to support minimum qualifications. The following information should be provided in your resume, but it is acceptable to provide elsewhere in your application package: employer's name, starting and end dates (Mo/Yr), hours per week, and pay plan, series and grade level (e.g. GS-0201-09) for relevant federal experience. TIP: A good way to ensure you include all essential information is to use the Resume Builder in USAJOBS to create your resume. Are you applying for a promotion? For GS positions, to be considered for promotion, you must provide SF-50(s) that shows you held the next lower GS grade for at least one year. SF-50s that have an effective date within the past year (e.g., General Adjustment SF-50 from this year or Within Rate/Grade Increases (WRI/WGI) SF-50 within a year) do not clearly show that you meet the one-year time-in-grade requirement. That means if you submit an SF-50 dated within the last year, you must submit another SF-50 that is dated more than one year ago to clearly demonstrate you meet the time-in-grade requirements. If you are a DoD employee, you can obtain a copy of your SF- 50(s) from MyBiz. Are you claiming membership in any professional organizations, or possession of a license, certificate or credentials? Check the Conditions of Employment section above to see if any are required. If you claim membership, license, certification, or credentials, you must submit a copy of said document in your application package. Are you using education as a substitute for some or all of the experience requirement? Is there a basic education requirement for this position? Check the Education section above to see what is allowed and what is required. Any claims you make in your resume or assessment questionnaire regarding education or degrees MUST be supported by submitting with your application official or unofficial transcripts or a list of courses, grades earned, completion dates, and quarter and semester hours earned issued from your school. While unofficial transcripts are acceptable for initial application, an official transcript will ultimately be required if you are selected for the position. You may submit a copy your degree(s) if specific coursework does not have to be verified. Are you a veteran claiming 5-point veterans' preference or claiming sole survivorship preference? You must submit a copy of your latest DD-214 Certificate of Release or Discharge from Active Duty (any copy that shows all dates of service, as well as character of service [Honorable, General, etc.] is acceptable) OR a VA letter that shows dates of service or service connected disability AND character of service. If you have more than one DD-214 for multiple periods of active duty service, submit a copy for each period of service. If you were issued a DD-215 to amend aforementioned information on the DD-214 you must submit that too. If you are not sure of your preference eligibility, visit the Department of Labor's website: Veterans' Preference Advisor Are you a disabled veteran or claiming 10-point veterans' preference? If you are eligible to claim 10 point veterans preference you must submit a DD-214 Certificate of Release or Discharge from Active Duty as described above for 5-point preference. You must also provide the applicable supporting documentation of your disability (e.g. disability letter from the VA) as described on Standard Form-15 (SF-15). http://www.opm.gov/forms/pdf_fill/SF15.pdf. Are you an active duty service member? Active Duty Service Members are required to submit a statement of service printed on command letterhead and signed by the command. The statement of service must provide the branch of service, rate/rank, all dates of service, the expected date of discharge and anticipated character of service (Honorable, General, etc.). Documents submitted as part of the application package, to include supplemental documents, may be shared beyond the Human Resources Office. Some supplemental documents contain personal information such as SSN and DOB and some documents such as military orders and marriage certificates may contain personal information for someone other than you. You may sanitize these documents to remove said personal information before you submit your application. You must provide an un-sanitized version of the documents if you are selected.

Specialized experience is defined as experience that is typically in or related to the work of the position to be filled including: advising leadership on performance/portfolio management at the treatment facility, Regional/Market, or headquarters level; selecting the appropriate methodology gap identification, project selection, scoping, and chartering; using business processing tools and statistical analysis to develop project execution plans (GS-12). You will be evaluated on the basis of your level of competency in the following areas: Administration and Management Leadership Planning and Evaluating Technical Competence Time in Grade Requirement: Applicants who have held a General Schedule (GS) position within the last 52 weeks must have 52 weeks of Federal service at the next lower grade or equivalent (GS-12).

Details.JobSummary: About the Position: This position is located within the Defense Health Agency (DHA) in Falls Church, VA under the policy guidance and direction of the Assistant Secretary of Defense for Health Affairs (ASD (HA)). A Lean Six Sigma Black Belt (LSS BB) DoD certification is HIGHLY PREFERRED. Please provide a copy with your application package.
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: At the Defense Health Agency (DHA), our Mission is to support the National Defense Strategy and Service Military Departments by leading the Military Health System (MHS) as an integrated, highly reliable system of medical training, readiness, and health. As the health care delivery arm of the MHS, DHA is crucial to supporting the Department of Defense's integrated system of readiness and health. DHA manages a global health care network of military and civilian medical professionals and more than 400 military hospitals and clinics around the world. DHA is a joint, integrated Combat Support Agency that enables the Army, Navy, and Air Force medical services to provide a medically ready force and ready medical force to Combatant Commands in both peacetime and wartime. The DHA supports the delivery of integrated, affordable, and high quality health services to the MHS beneficiaries and is responsible for driving greater integration of clinical and business processes across the MHS.
MajorDuties: Providing technical expertise and program support in the creation, program management, and sustainment of a Continuous Process Improvement.
Identify performance metrics in which organizations are failing to meet expectations.
Assist leaders with selecting and executing applicable projects tailored to improve performance in areas of command emphasis.
Provides technical direction in areas of project management, team building, and facilitation.
Integrate improvement efforts with strategic and operational command priorities.

Details.JobSummary: About the Position: This position supports the mission of J-8, Financial Operations Directorate in the Financial Operations Division and is located in Falls Church, VA. Student Loan repayment may be authorized.
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: At the Defense Health Agency (DHA), our Mission is to support the National Defense Strategy and Service Military Departments by leading the Military Health System (MHS) as an integrated, highly reliable system of medical training, readiness, and health. As the health care delivery arm of the MHS, DHA is crucial to supporting the Department of Defense's integrated system of readiness and health. DHA manages a global health care network of military and civilian medical professionals and more than 400 military hospitals and clinics around the world. DHA is a joint, integrated Combat Support Agency that enables the Army, Navy, and Air Force medical services to provide a medically ready force and ready medical force to Combatant Commands in both peacetime and wartime. The DHA supports the delivery of integrated, affordable, and high quality health services to the MHS beneficiaries and is responsible for driving greater integration of clinical and business processes across the MHS.
MajorDuties: Serve as a Management and Program Analyst within the DHA, Financial Operations Division (FOD).
Formulate and staffs operating policies and procedures and ensures that all instructions issued to the division are in accordance with the Director's policies and plans.
Assume Financial System and Civilian Payroll (FSCP) Chief responsibilities in his/her absence.
Participate and assist Financial Operations Division (FOD) leadership in planning and coordinating short-term, mid-term, and long-range activities of the Division.
Link FOD objectives to the MHS enterprise vision, mission, goals, objectives and priorities.

MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: In order to qualify, you must meet the specialized experience requirements described in the Office of Personnel Management (OPM) Qualification Standards for General Schedule Positions, Administrative and Management Positions. SPECIALIZED EXPERIENCE: Applicants must have at least one (1) year of specialized experience at the next lower grade GS-13, or equivalent in other pay systems. Examples of specialized experience includes comprehensive knowledge of Departmental and Service policies, regulations, directives, and issues related to senior and executive-level military and civilian personnel management that includes internal and Service-wide organizational structure, management policies, procedures, and practices. FEDERAL TIME-IN-GRADE (TIG) REQUIREMENT FOR GENERAL SCHEDULE (GS) POSITIONS: Merit promotion applicants must meet applicable time-in­-grade requirements to be considered eligible. One year at the GS-13 level is required to meet the time-in-grade requirements for the GS-14 level. TIG applies if you are in a current GS position or held a GS position within the previous 52 weeks. NOTE: Applicants applying as VEOA candidates who are current GS civil service employees or are prior GS civil service employees within the past 52 weeks must also meet time-in-grade requirements. KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS AND ABILITIES (KSAs): Your qualifications will be evaluated on the basis of your level of knowledge, skills, abilities and/or competencies in the following areas: 1. Expert knowledge of wide area of military and civilian senior leader personnel management programs, initiatives, polices, and practices that enable the incumbent to serve as an expert in the full range of personnel, manpower and organization functions as well as the ability to incorporate necessary training/program initiatives that meet mission requirements. 2. Knowledge of force management and career field management programs including guidance, policies, procedures, and directives. Must possess general knowledge of principles and practices of force management to carryout responsibilities and provide decision support to respective leaders. 3. Knowledge of safety and security regulations, practices and procedures. 4. Skills to plan, organize and complete work to meet program and AF and AFMS objectives. Skill and ability to speak and write effectively on highly complex issues prepared for senior military officials. Ability to conduct presentations, chair meetings, lead task forces, and prepare reports at the General Officer/SES level. 5. Skilled in fostering collaborative relationships both within and outside the organization to develop multi-organizational team studies. Ability to communicate orally and in writing, clearly, concisely, timely, and with technical accuracy to a high level audience 6. Ability to deal with personnel and agencies in situations that requires tact and diplomacy. Skills required and experience desired in dealing with a customer base of colonels, General Officers, Senior Executives and Political Appointees. PART-TIME OR UNPAID EXPERIENCE: Credit will be given for appropriate unpaid and or part-time work. You must clearly identify the duties and responsibilities in each position held and the total number of hours per week. VOLUNTEER WORK EXPERIENCE: Refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service Programs (i.e., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community; student and social). Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge and skills that can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment. You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience.

Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: The mission of the United States Air Force is: To fly, fight, and win ... Airpower anytime, anywhere. To achieve that mission, the Air Force has a vision of Global Vigilance, Global Reach and Global Power. That vision orbits around three core competencies: Developing Airmen, Technology-to-Warfighting and Integrating Operations. Core competencies and distinctive capabilities are based on a shared commitment to three core values -- integrity first, service before self, and excellence in all we do. Click here to view the AF Civilian Employment Eligibility Guide: 30 Percent or More Disabled Veterans AF DCIPS Interchange AF Internal Employee DoD Transfer (Excluding Air Force) EO 12721 Certain Former Overseas Employees EO 13473 Appointment of Certain Military Spouses Former Federal Employees (Reinstatement) Interagency Career Transition Assistance Plan Land Management Employee Military Spouse Preference National Service (Peace Corps and VISTA) Non-AF DCIPS Interchange Non-Appropriated Fund Non-DoD Transfer Other (Interchange Agreements) People with Disabilities, Schedule A Veterans Employment Opportunities Act
MajorDuties: Develops, implements and provides guidance on policies, programs and procedures for the development of AFMS high potential colonels. Leads internal teams to develop policies, instructions and materials as needed for effective and consistent management of high potential AFMS Colonels in the United States Air Force. Manages strategic and technical guidance as senior advisor to AF/SG on all aspects of senior/executive leader management programs. Subject matter expert for AFMS senior leader management programs with responsibilities for all personnel actions associated with approximately 900 senior leaders requiring interaction with HAF, SAF, Major Commands and all Combatant Commands. Provides oversight for career field management program considerations, career progression, training, assignments, and career management actions. Represents the AF/SG and AFMS Senior Leadership at DoD, Air Force, MAJCOM, COCOM, or functional meetings on topics as it pertains to AFMS Senior Leader Management and Career Field Force Managements. Serves as the AFMS executive agent for colonels and colonel selects for AF Central Selection Boards and AFMS Senior Leader Development Programs and Awards. Tasks AFMS Functional leaders, MAJCOM SGs and colonels assigned to their command to submit board member candidates in terms of the required board composition.
Details.Education: ********************ADDITIONAL INFORMATION FOR ACTIVE DUTY SERVICES MEMBERS******************** ACTIVE DUTY SERVICE MEMBERS: The VOW Act requires federal agencies to treat an eligible active duty service member as a veteran, disabled veteran, and preference eligible (as applicable) when applying for civil service positions before the effective release or discharge date. Appointment of military members before the release or discharge date is permissible if the member is on terminal leave. At the time the active duty member applies for a civil position, he or she must submit a "certification" memo in lieu of a DD-Form 214, Certificate of Release or Discharge from Active Duty. Active duty members applying for a civil service position without submitting a valid certification memo or DD-Form 214 with their application will render the member ineligible for the position. The certification memo must originate from the member's military service branch on official letterhead and contain the following: Name/Rank/Grade of Service Member Branch of Armed Forces Dates of Active Service (Start and End Date(s) Expected Date of Discharge/Release from Active Duty Terminal leave start date (if applicable) Expected character of service (honorable or general) and type of separation (i.e. separation or retirement) Must be certified within 120 days of anticipated discharge Signature by, or by direction of the adjutant, personnel office, unit commander, or higher headquarters commander. Note: The VOW Act provides tentative preference. If appointed, a DD Form-214 must be submitted upon receipt

Details.JobSummary: You will serve as a SUPERVISORY CORRESPONDENCE MANAGEMENT in the Directorate for Administration of BUREAU OF MEDICINE. This is a RE-ADVERTISEMENT of Announcement Number: ST-11771219-23-KEB. Applicants that have previously applied NEED to re-apply to this announcement.
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: The Navy and Marine Corps team offers innovative, exciting and meaningful work linking military and civilian talents to achieve our mission and safeguard our freedoms. Department of the Navy provides competitive salaries, comprehensive benefits, and extensive professional development and training. From pipefitters to accountants, scientists to engineers, doctors to nurses-the careers and opportunities to make a difference are endless. Civilian careers-where purpose and patriotism unite!
MajorDuties: You will serve as an advisor to the Director, Secretariat and Assistant Chief of Staff on all matters related to inquiries and correspondence.
You will serve as the Program Manager for enterprise Knowledge Management (eKM) system.

You will be the instructor to BUMED staff on proper package preparation to higher authority for all BUMED assignments ensuring correct format and writing is clear and concise before submission for signature.
You will manage an internal (eKM) and external (HQWeb) unclassified and classified tasker tickler systems database providing daily reports and status on more than 240 taskers.
You will develop and conduct didactic instruction to all BUMED Headquarters directors and action officers, as well as four Navy Medicine Regions on the use of the eKM system.

You will provide oversight of all incoming taskers from members of the House and Senate, Offices of the Secretary of Defense, TRICARE Management Activity, Offices of the Joint Chiefs of Staff and several other personnel.

As described above, your complete application includes your resume, your responses to the online questionnaire, and documents which prove your eligibility to apply. If you fail to provide these documents, you will be marked as having an incomplete application package and you will not be considered any further. 1. Your resume: Your resume may be submitted in any format and must support the specialized experience described in this announcement. If your resume includes a photograph or other inappropriate material or content, it will not be used to make eligibility and qualification determinations and you may not be considered for this vacancy. For qualifications determinations your resume must contain hours worked per week and the dates of employment (i.e., HRS per week and month/year to month/year or month/year to present). If your resume does not contain this information, your application may be marked as incomplete and you may not receive consideration for this position. For additional information see: What to include in your resume. 2. Other supporting documents: Cover Letter, optional Most recent Performance Appraisal, if applicable Proof of Eligibility to Apply: Your application must include the documents which prove you are eligible to apply for the vacancy. The Proof of Eligibility document describes authorities commonly used in merit promotion recruitment and what document(s) are required to prove you meet the requirements of the authority. You must meet the requirements of at least one of the authorities listed in the Who May Apply section above to receive further consideration. Time-in-grade documentation: If you are applying for a higher grade and your SF-50 has an effective date within the past year, it may not clearly demonstrate you meet the one year time-in-grade requirement so you will need to provide an SF-50 which clearly demonstrates you meet the time-in-grade requirements (examples of appropriate SF-50s include Promotions, Within-grade Grade/Range Increases, and SF-50s with an effective date more than one year old). NOTE: Documents submitted as part of the application package, to include supplemental documents, may be shared beyond the Human Resources Office. Some supplemental documents such as military orders and marriage certificates may contain personal information for someone other than you. You may sanitize these documents to remove another person's personal information before you submit your application. You may be asked to provide an un-sanitized version of the documents if you are selected to confirm your eligibility.
Details.OtherInformation: Male applicants born after December 31, 1959, must complete a Pre-Employment Certification Statement for Selective Service Registration. You will be required to provide proof of U.S. Citizenship. One year trial/probationary period may be required. Direct deposit of pay is required. Selection is subject to restrictions resulting from Department of Defense referral system for displaced employees. MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: In order to qualify for the GS-11, your resume must demonstrate at least one year of specialized experience at or equivalent to the (GS-09) grade level or pay band in the Federal service or equivalent experience in the private or public sector. Specialized experience must demonstrate the following: Experience utilizing qualitative and quantitative techniques for analyzing/evaluating the effectiveness, efficiency and productivity of human capital programs; Experience communicating effectively both written and oral, (i.e. not to exclude conducting detailed analysis of complex Total Force systems and/or organized and succinct prepared point papers/staff reports ? presenting findings in informal and formal briefings to peers and senior leaders, etc?); Experience gathering information, identifying and analyzing interrelated manpower management issues of effectiveness and efficiency to resolve potential manpower related problems; Experience using automated data systems/sources such as Total Force Manpower Management System (TFMMS) and Defense Medical Human Resource System internet (DMHRSI) to gather and analyze manpower data; AND Experience analyzing quantity/quality reports ensuring that they accurately reflect approved Future Years Defense Plan (FYDP) shifts. Additional qualification information can be found from the following Office of Personnel Management web site: http://www.opm.gov/qualifications/Standards/group-stds/gs-admin.asp. https://www.opm.gov/policy-data-oversight/classification-qualifications/general-schedule-qualification-standards/0300/management-and-program-analysis-series-0343/ Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., professional, philanthropic, religious, spiritual, community, student, social). Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge, and skills and can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment.

Details.JobSummary: You will serve as a PROGRAM ANALYST in the Total Force Operations Division of BUREAU OF MEDICINE.
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: The Navy and Marine Corps team offers innovative, exciting and meaningful work linking military and civilian talents to achieve our mission and safeguard our freedoms. Department of the Navy provides competitive salaries, comprehensive benefits, and extensive professional development and training. From pipefitters to accountants, scientists to engineers, doctors to nurses-the careers and opportunities to make a difference are endless. Civilian careers-where purpose and patriotism unite!
MajorDuties: You will provide manpower human capital management analysis using multiple data systems and manages total force manpower for all BUMED, Budget Submitting Offices (BSO) 18 activities.
You will investigate, review, evaluate, and make recommendations on methods for management and allocation of military, civilian, and contract manpower resources.
You will advise on course of action to achieve more effective and efficient use of limited manpower resources in the delivery of health care services in an operational environment.
You will identify manpower areas for improvement with BUMED organizations and assess the scope, complexity, and risk of the issue.
You will uses Data sources include, but are not limited to, Total Force Manpower Management System (TFMMS), and Fleet Training Management and Planning System (FLTMPS).
You will work within a military setting and/or military medicine.

(Possession of the requirements must be verifiable via SUBMITTING A COPY of the complete transcripts with your application.) or Successful completion three "3" full years of progressively higher level graduate education leading to such a degree (Possession of the requirements must be verifiable via SUBMITTING A COPY of the complete transcripts with your application.) or Successful completion LL.M., if related (Possession of the requirements must be verifiable via SUBMITTING A COPY of the complete transcripts with your application.) From pipefitters to accountants, scientists to engineers, doctors to nurses-the careers and opportunities to make a difference are endless. Details.JobSummary: About the Position: This position is with the 3rd Medical Deployment Support Command(MDSC), G-3/5/7, 3 Mission Support Element located in Forest Park, Georgia. Description of the Working Environment: Work is performed in an office setting.
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: Civilian employees serve a vital role in supporting the Army mission. They provide the skills that are not readily available in the military, but crucial to support military operations. The Army integrates the talents and skills of its military and civilian members to form a Total Army. The Army values diversity of perspectives, backgrounds, cultures and skills, which connects employees to organizations that are committed to building an inclusive work environment where they can contribute to their fullest potential.
MajorDuties: Develop training plans and schedules
Inspects training schedules and objectives
Establishes security procedures
Monitors funds for command
Developing, implementing, and appraising plans and schedules for the Division Training Program
Analyzing regulations, tactical doctrine, field manuals, and issuances pertaining to training objectives and determining training needs of the Division
Evaluating training operations through inspections or reviews of reports and issuing directives to effect improvement
Reviewing plans and evaluating training of subordinate elements
Advising the Division on training matters
Establishing and recommending priority and commitment of resources projected and available for personnel, equipment and facilities

MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: Eligibility for this position will be based on clear and comprehensive showing that the applicant has had experience of the scope and quality sufficient to carry out the duties and assignments of the position. Additionally, applicants must possess the essential skills, knowledge, and abilities listed in the Executive Core Qualifications and Technical Qualifications paragraphs below. EXECUTIVE CORE QUALIFICATIONS (ECQs) Leading Change: The ability to bring about strategic change, both within and outside the organization, to meet organizational goals. Inherent to this ECQ is the ability to establish an organizational vision and to implement it in a continuously changing environment. Leading People: The ability to lead people toward meeting the organization's vision, mission, and goals. Inherent to this ECQ is the ability to provide an inclusive workplace that fosters the development of others, facilitates cooperation and teamwork, and supports constructive resolution of conflicts. Results Driven: The ability to meet organizational goals and customer expectations. Inherent to this ECQ is the ability to make decisions that produce high quality results by applying technical knowledge, analyzing problems, and calculating risks. Business Acumen: The ability to manage human, financial, and information resources strategically. Building Coalitions: The ability to build coalitions internally and with other Federal agencies, State and local governments, nonprofit and private sector organizations, foreign governments, or international organizations to achieve common goals. In addition, DoD requires the Enterprise Perspective: The ability to apply a broad point of view and an understanding of individual or organizational responsibilities in relation to DoD or government-wide strategic priorities is required. Executives must demonstrate ability to work with internal and external partners to support national security objectives. This perspective is typically gained through a variety of diverse work experiences. A separate narrative statement is not required. This information should be embedded within the application package (Resume, Technical Qualifications and Executive Core Qualifications). TECHNICAL QUALIFICATIONS (TQs): Experience in leading enterprise level logistics business process management in the areas of order fulfillment, planning, tech/quality, and supply chain management in support of wholesale and retail customers Ability to direct a robust sales and operations planning (S&OP) process in order to link supply and demand through customer collaboration and advanced inventory management techniques. Ability to optimize use material obligation authority by analyzing various level setting/support options (e.g. lead-times, forecast accuracy, safety stock) prior to their implementation.

Details.JobSummary: This position serves as the Executive Director, Logistics Policy and Programs, for the Defense Logistics Agency (DLA) Logistics Operations directorate (J3). DLA, a multimission, Joint Chiefs of Staff-designated combat support agency, employs almost 27,000 civilian and military personnel geographically dispersed in the Continental United States and abroad.
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: The DLA mission is to furnish effective and efficient worldwide logistics support to the Military Departments, other DoD components, as well as to other Federal agencies, foreign agencies, foreign governments, and international organizations during peacetime, contingencies, and wartime operations. In the execution of the mission, DLA manages eight supply chains and nearly 6.1 million items in support of more than 2,400 weapon systems with an inventory value of over $20 billion through its integrated procurement, supply depot distribution, and reutilization systems, supported by automated business systems and technological infrastructure investments of over $1.8 billion annually. The position supports and serves as principal advisor to the Agency's Director, through the Director, J3, in the areas of overall logistics management. Provides oversight for Material Policy, Process and Assessment, Strategic Programs and Initiatives. The Executive Director provides executive leadership in integrating and synchronizing the key business and supply chain management functions. This position is in the Senior Executive Service, a small elite group of top government leaders. SES members possess a diverse portfolio of experiences including strong skills to lead across organizations. As an executive you will influence the direction of innovation and transformation of the federal government and lead the next generation of public servants.
MajorDuties: This position ensures availability of consistent and auditable Agency capabilities.

Manages the Agency's sales and operations planning (S and OP) process to align resources across the Agency's demand and supply chains to ensure customer support outcomes are achieved with optimal efficiency.
The incumbent is responsible for refining planning process parameters (e.g. Safety stock, coverage durations, etc.) to ensure optimal support to the warfighter.
The incumbent will ensure that Alternatives to Forecasting methods are utilized in instances where forecasting proves to be a less efficient method to achieve a given level of effectiveness.
The Executive Director is responsible for all related directorate transformation initiatives and interface with associated Agency transformation programs.
The Executive Director exercises oversight and management of the Enterprise-wide internal processes required to deliver value-added logistics solutions to the warfighters.
These processes include stabilizing and improving order fulfillment, planning, and technical/quality processes across the enterprise for all demand and supply chains.

The incumbent of this position provides continuity of operations and functional expertise across a broad range of business responsibilities which are critical to the long-term mission success of DLA as a supplier of logistics good and services.
The Executive Director is responsible for extending competencies and capabilities of the Agency closer to the warfighter through retail integration stabilization and growth.
The incumbent makes broad policy decisions, which have far-ranging effects on customer support and sustainment support throughout the DoD.

The incumbent is accountable and responsible for the assigned program(s) to include development, documentation, and operation of both internal processes and administrative controls that are auditable and repeatable.
The incumbent is responsible for Enterprise integration of strategic programs and initiatives led from within the Directorate.

The incumbent is responsible for management and control of Directorate business and resource management, administration and all operations associated with the supervision, planning and management of the Logistics Policy and Programs Directorate.
The incumbent identifies issues and provides alternative solutions or courses of action to governing authorities (General Officer level).

DRUG-FREE WORKPLACE: The Defense Logistics Agency (DLA) has established a Drug-Free Federal Workplace Policy. All applicants tentatively selected for DLA employment in a testing designated position are subject to urinalysis to screen for illegal drug use prior to appointment. Applicants who refuse to be tested will be denied employment with DLA for a period of six months. This policy extends to random testing for the use of illegal drugs by employees who occupy testing designated positions defined as sensitive in Section 7(d) of Executive Order 12564. The Defense Logistics Agency's Drug Free Workplace Plan's drug testing panel includes testing for the following illegal substances: marijuana, cocaine, opiates (codeine/morphine), 6-Acetylmorphine (heroin), phencyclidine, amphetamines (amphetamine/methamphetamine), methylenedioxymethamphetamine (MDMA), methylenedioxyamphetamine (MDA), oxycodone, oxymorphone, hydrocodone, and hydromorphone.

Details.JobSummary: This position is part of the Defense Threat Reduction Agency. The incumbent is responsible for planning, coordinating, integrating, implementing, and evaluating the use of acquisition programs in the broad area of Chemical and Biological Defense.
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: Our Mission: The Defense Threat Reduction Agency provides cross-cutting solutions to enable the DoD, the United States Government, and international partners to DETER strategic attack against the United States and it's allies; PREVENT, reduce, and counter Weapons of Mass Destruction (WMD) and emerging threats; and PREVAIL against WMD-armed adversaries in crisis and conflict.
MajorDuties: This position is being filled under DoD Direct Hire Auth 5 U.S.C. § 9905, 10/15/2021. As a PROGRAM MANAGER (DIAGNOSTICS AND DETECTION) at the GS-0340-13 some of your typical work assignments may include: Acquisition and program management knowledge, methods and techniques to identify, propose and implement solutions to management problems associated with difficult and unprecedented program issues that are difficult to foresee and which are scrutinized through a number of reviews at senior agency levels (DOD, other federal agencies, Congress, and international organizations). Advises Division Chief and Portfolio Leads on the management of financial resources to achieve DoD obligation and expenditure goals for the Diagnostics and Detection Program. Acquisition and financial knowledge in translating technical information into required programmatic and fiscal documentation to support the planning, programming, budgeting, and execution system for the Diagnostics and Detection Program. Provides guidance and advice to Division Chief and Science and Technology Managers in the conduct of market research and preparation, coordination and tracking of a wide variety of procurement request (PR) packages.

Details.SubAgencyName: Director for Administration, Dept of Ops & Emergency Mgt, Emergency Ops Center (EOC)
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: At the Defense Health Agency (DHA), our Mission is to support the National Defense Strategy and Service Military Departments by leading the Military Health System (MHS) as an integrated, highly reliable system of medical training, readiness, and health. As the health care delivery arm of the MHS, DHA is crucial to supporting the Department of Defense's integrated system of readiness and health. DHA manages a global health care network of military and civilian medical professionals and more than 400 military hospitals and clinics around the world. DHA is a joint, integrated Combat Support Agency that enables the Army, Navy, and Air Force medical services to provide a medically ready force and ready medical force to Combatant Commands in both peacetime and wartime. The DHA supports the delivery of integrated, affordable, and high quality health services to the MHS beneficiaries and is responsible for driving greater integration of clinical and business processes across the MHS.
MajorDuties: Develop, coordinate, and monitor operation plans and orders in support of defined requirements and objectives.
Participate in internal and external operational planning, identifies courses of action to meet mission requirements, anticipates problems or conflicts.
Perform emergency response procedures which includes data/ information management, such as preparing duty/communication logs, technical briefings, task/resource lists, and correspondence.
Assist with the development of exercise objectives, master scenario event lists, control plans, transportation plans, and support requirements/plans for drills and exercises.
Establish dates for analysis and submission of requisition for maintenance to acquisition management.
Inspect equipment to ensure recall/warning/alert corrections have been performed.
Perform assessments to determine risk assessment to equipment management including biomedical equipment.
Assist in the development of hospital issuances (e.g., instructions and manuals) related to section?s core functions.
Assist in performing complex projects in support of higher headquarters and organization-specific operations with special emphasis on Commander?s Critical Information Requirements.
Extract intelligence and applicable information from classified and unclassified sources to identify operational impacts.
Process and coordinate service-specific tasking and deployment requirements received by a variety of communication channels to include applicable automated systems.

MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: GENERAL QUALIFICATIONS: General education and/or experience requirements described in the Office of Personnel Management (OPM) Qualification Standards for Administrative and Management positions. SPECIALIZED EXPERIENCE: One (1) year of specialized experience at the next lower broadband, NH-03, equivalent to the next lower grade, GS-13 or equivalent, in other personnel pay systems including experience in the actual type of work for which application is made. Specialized experience is: Experience identifying communication needs and developing informational materials that inform appropriate and varied audiences of the organization's policies, programs, services and activities. Experience evaluating the effectiveness of information and communication programs in furthering organizational goals. Experience advising senior leaders and management on policy formulation and potential public reaction to proposed policy. Experience with designing and developing informational materials for both the general public and targeted audiences. Experience establishing and maintaining effective working relationships with all media, and internal and external customers. Experience with planning, initiating and implementing comprehensive public affairs and strategic communication campaigns. Experience with advising senior level management on the organization's various communication programs, plans and issues. Experience with application of marketing/partnership principles, methods, and techniques and the ability to apply that knowledge with a high degree of resourcefulness, ingenuity and creativity. Includes the knowledge to segment target markets, identify specific characteristics, and determine the most effective marketing techniques to influence them. PART-TIME OR UNPAID EXPERIENCE: Credit will be given for appropriate unpaid and or part-time work. You must clearly identify the duties and responsibilities in each position held and the total number of hours per week. VOLUNTEER WORK EXPERIENCE: Refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service Programs (i.e., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community; student and social). Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge and skills that can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment. You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience.

Details.JobSummary: This position is under the DoD Acquisition Workforce Personnel Demonstration Project (AcqDemo) within Title 5 Competitive Service. For more information on Acq Demo please go to the DoD AcqDemo website at https://acqdemo.hci.mil/ and Fact Sheet at https://acqdemo.hci.mil/faq.html
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: Join DAU and be a part of a world-class Department of Defense organization committed to training and supporting Defense acquisition professionals. In addition to training courses, DAU offers a variety of learning events and experiences, provides tools and resources to help on the job, conducts direct assistance to organizations, and offers access to an entire community of practitioners, experts and policy makers. DAU promotes a culture of lifelong learning both for faculty and staff and for the members of the Defense Acquisition Workforce they serve. Join our dynamic team and help give our military the competitive advantage they need.
MajorDuties: Responsible for developing, coordinating, executing, and evaluating an integrated communication strategy and overall program in support of all DAU activities including those of the business units. The program goals consist of an outreach campaign that informs the workforce of product development, activities, services, and capabilities available through the DAU platform. Duties include but are not limited to the following: Works closely with the director of communications and public affairs to plan and organize strategic communication efforts in support of DoD acquisition policy, initiatives and communication strategies as they relate to the DAU mission, its projects, programs and strategies. Helps develop top level messages, themes and products in support of DoD, Undersecretary of Defense (Acquisition and Sustainment) and DAU goals. Provides continual analysis of ongoing outreach initiatives to identify areas for improvement and makes recommendations for adjustment in both short and long range communications planning and programs. Proactively seeks opportunities for extending the reach of communication efforts. Conducts research regarding customer perceptions, defines needs and creates benchmarks to measure success. Identifies emerging issues and targets of opportunity that may arise. Advises senior leaders on metrics development, feedback process management, customer focus, and strategic performance indicators. Works to develop new ways of gathering meaningful input to develop more effective communications strategies and improve understanding of DAU's mission, activities, available products and services, as well as achievements and accomplishments. Serves as a subject matter expert for outreach, communication, marketing, and information sharing, exercising overall responsibility for developing and implementing a comprehensive strategy aimed at communicating the DAU mission and messaging to a variety of federal, military, and commercial audiences. Plans, creates, implements, coordinates, and directs a comprehensive program designed to inform and influence key decision makers in the military, federal and corporate arenas. Informs and trains other personnel in the proper development, implementation, and utilization of market research information, outreach and marketing plans, exhibit design and development, and promotional materials.

MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: SPECIALIZED EXPERIENCE: One (1) year of specialized experience at the next lower broadband, NH-03, equivalent to the next lower grade, GS-13 or equivalent, in other personnel pay systems including experience in the actual type of work for which application is made. Specialized experience is: Experience identifying communication needs and developing informational materials that inform appropriate and varied audiences of the organization's policies, programs, services and activities. Experience evaluating the effectiveness of information and communication programs in furthering organizational goals. Experience advising senior leaders and management on policy formulation and potential public reaction to proposed policy. Experience with designing and developing informational materials for both the general public and targeted audiences. Experience establishing and maintaining effective working relationships with all media, and internal and external customers. Experience with planning, initiating and implementing comprehensive public affairs and strategic communication campaigns. Experience with advising senior level management on the organization's various communication programs, plans and issues. Experience with application of marketing/partnership principles, methods, and techniques and the ability to apply that knowledge with a high degree of resourcefulness, ingenuity and creativity. Includes the knowledge to segment target markets, identify specific characteristics, and determine the most effective marketing techniques to influence them. PART-TIME OR UNPAID EXPERIENCE: Credit will be given for appropriate unpaid and or part-time work. You must clearly identify the duties and responsibilities in each position held and the total number of hours per week. VOLUNTEER WORK EXPERIENCE: Refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service Programs (i.e., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community; student and social). Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge and skills that can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment. You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience.

Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: Join DAU and be a part of a world-class Department of Defense organization committed to training and supporting Defense acquisition professionals. In addition to training courses, DAU offers a variety of learning events and experiences, provides tools and resources to help on the job, conducts direct assistance to organizations, and offers access to an entire community of practitioners, experts and policy makers. DAU promotes a culture of lifelong learning both for faculty and staff and for the members of the Defense Acquisition Workforce they serve. Join our dynamic team and help give our military the competitive advantage they need.
MajorDuties: Responsible for developing, coordinating, executing, and evaluating an integrated communication strategy and overall program in support of all DAU activities including those of the business units. The program goals consist of an outreach campaign that informs the workforce of product development, activities, services, and capabilities available through the DAU platform. Duties include but are not limited to the following: Works closely with the director of communications and public affairs to plan and organize strategic communication efforts in support of DoD acquisition policy, initiatives and communication strategies as they relate to the DAU mission, its projects, programs and strategies. Helps develop top level messages, themes and products in support of DoD, Undersecretary of Defense (Acquisition and Sustainment) and DAU goals. Provides continual analysis of ongoing outreach initiatives to identify areas for improvement and makes recommendations for adjustment in both short and long range communications planning and programs. Proactively seeks opportunities for extending the reach of communication efforts. Conducts research regarding customer perceptions, defines needs and creates benchmarks to measure success. Identifies emerging issues and targets of opportunity that may arise. Advises senior leaders on metrics development, feedback process management, customer focus, and strategic performance indicators. Works to develop new ways of gathering meaningful input to develop more effective communications strategies and improve understanding of DAU's mission, activities, available products and services, as well as achievements and accomplishments. Serves as a subject matter expert for outreach, communication, marketing, and information sharing, exercising overall responsibility for developing and implementing a comprehensive strategy aimed at communicating the DAU mission and messaging to a variety of federal, military, and commercial audiences. Plans, creates, implements, coordinates, and directs a comprehensive program designed to inform and influence key decision makers in the military, federal and corporate arenas. Informs and trains other personnel in the proper development, implementation, and utilization of market research information, outreach and marketing plans, exhibit design and development, and promotional materials.

MatchedObjectDescriptor.PositionTitle: MISSION SUPPORT SPECIALIST (LOGISTICS TRAINING AND TRAVEL)
MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: You may qualify at the GS-12, if you fulfill the following qualifications: One year of specialized experience equivalent to the GS-11 grade level in the Federal service: Knowledge of logistics, training and travel fields with the Department of Defense or for a major civilian corporation. Ability to communicate concisely, both orally and in writing, to direct, explain, guide, and recommend solutions for a wide range of training and travel requirements and concepts to leadership. Knowledge of support mission requirements in all areas of base support. Familiar with defense travel system (DTS) or equivalent travel or accounting systems to maintain data accuracy and ensure compliance with government regulations. You may qualify at the GS-13, if you fulfill the following qualifications: One year of specialized experience equivalent to the GS-12 grade level in the Federal service: Expert experience in the logistics, training and travel fields with the Department of Defense or for a major civilian corporation. Ability to communicate concisely, both orally and in writing, to direct, explain, guide, and recommend solutions for a wide range of training and travel requirements and concepts to leadership. Expert knowledge of support mission requirements in all areas of base support. Expert Knowledge of safety and security regulations, practices, and procedures. Skilled in the defense travel system (DTS) or equivalent travel or accounting systems to maintain data accuracy and ensure compliance with government regulations. Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community, student, social). Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge, and skills and can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment. You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience.

Details.JobSummary: This position is part of the Defense Threat Reduction Agency.
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: The Defense Threat Reduction Agency provides cross-cutting solutions to enable the DoD, the United States Government, and international partners to DETER strategic attack against the United States and it's allies; PREVENT, reduce, and counter Weapons of Mass Destruction (WMD) and emerging threats; and PREVAIL against WMD-armed adversaries in crisis and conflict
MajorDuties: As a MISSION SUPPORT SPECIALIST (LOGISTICS TRAINING AND TRAVEL) at the GS-0301-12/13 some of your typical work assignments may include: The incumbent works under the supervision of the Support Division for the Chief, Mission Assurance Department (a military O-6) and directly coordinates readiness, mandatory, and professional development training for 80 government and military personnel (GS-13 and above and E-7 through O-6) and 220 contract personnel. Develops training related policies and procedures for the department based upon agency and other guidance. Works with the Training and Integration personnel in developing the department's training standard operating procedure. Assists with the development of the quarterly and annual training agenda. Incumbent directly impacts the capabilities, readiness, and professional competence of the Joint Mission Assurance Assessment (JMAA), Balanced Survivability Assessment (BSA), DoD Red teams and Advance Cyber Assessment Tools (ACAT) by ensuring key scientific and technical personnel are trained on the most current and relevant tactics, techniques, and procedures for their area of expertise. In addition, ensures assessment team personnel are capable of world-wide deployment, including hazardous duty areas. Incumbent ensures assessment and mobile training teams are appropriately equipped to accomplish their mission. Independently develops and manages the organization's training and equipment accountability programs. Establishes criteria and schedules to attain training goals and objectives. Explains the Agency and Department's policy and guidelines to new employees. Assists new employees with registration in the Learning Management System (LMS) and schedules personnel for training courses identified as mandatory for agency employees. Establishes a tracking mechanism to ensure all assigned personnel complete required training. Provides quarterly feedback on training records to the supervisors. Processes approved training requests using the established workflow to ensure timelines are met. Monitors the department's training budget and keeps leadership apprised. Coordinates readiness requirements with the Deployment Readiness Cell. Works closely with the Readiness Cell to coordinate training events conducive to the JMAA Schedule. Ensures personnel complete all required training in order to maintain world-wide deployable. Ensures the department's training plans are consistent with the DTRA's Training and Strategic Plans. The incumbent oversees all aspects of the department's equipment management program, including accountability, issue, receipt, research, and maintenance. Through coordination with assigned equipment custodians, defines the baseline equipment issue for each assigned team. Coordinates equipment issue for new personnel through the Acquisition and Logistics. Ensures military members are outfitted with the proper military uniforms with all accoutrements. Plans for and manages systems, subsystems, and equipment throughout their life cycle, including integrated logistics support activities. Develops, initiates, integrates, and manages all logistics actions associated with life cycle management of equipment. Serves as logistics focal point throughout the system's life cycle. Formulates logistics management and fiscal policy for division high value equipment. Analyzes the demand for supplies and forecasts future needs to ensure adequate supplies and equipment are on-hand to support mission needs. Manages the inspection, shipping, handling, and packaging of supplies and equipment to include return of defective equipment for repair. Establishes and monitors warranties on high value items. Evaluates bids and proposals submitted by potential suppliers and recommends the best product that meets the division's needs and is the most cost effective. Maintains accountability for supplies and equipment. Resolves problems related to storage, safety, and other hazards. Manages storage space utilization and develops and maintains a storage facility to include maintenance, future upgrades, and working stock requirements. Schedules and coordinates movement of equipment by commercial or military modes when required. Makes travel arrangements for deploying team members, including military airlift, if required; coordinates passport requirements through coordination with U.S. State Department and Embassies, billeting, ground transportation, country/theatre clearances, and coordinates any assessment-specific requirements. Prepares operations orders/travel authorizations for each deployment of division personnel to conduct assessments or training. The incumbent assumes a leadership role in establishing criterion for the department's mission specialists and enacts policies/procedures to accomplish established objectives. Reviews applicants for mission support specialists' vacancies within the department, provides prioritized selection, conducts interviews.

Makes travel arrangements; coordinates passport requirements through coordination with U.S. State Department and Embassies, billeting, ground transportation, country/theatre clearances, and coordinates any assessment-specific requirements. You may qualify at the GS-13 grade level, if you fulfill the following qualifications: One year of specialized experience equivalent to the GS-12 grade level in the Federal service: Develops training policies and procedures for mandatory and professional development training; Monitors the department's training budget and keeps leadership apprised; Analyzes the demand for supplies and forecasts future needs to ensure adequate supplies and equipment are on-hand to support mission needs; Makes travel arrangements; coordinates passport requirements through coordination with U.S. State Department and Embassies, billeting, ground transportation, country/theatre clearances, and coordinates any assessment-specific requirements. Details.JobSummary: This position is part of the Defense Threat Reduction Agency.
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: The Defense Threat Reduction Agency provides cross-cutting solutions to enable the DoD, the United States Government, and international partners to DETER strategic attack against the United States and it's allies; PREVENT, reduce, and counter Weapons of Mass Destruction (WMD) and emerging threats; and PREVAIL against WMD-armed adversaries in crisis and conflict.
MajorDuties: As a MISSION SUPPORT SPECIALIST (LOGISTICS TRAINING AND TRAVEL) at the GS-0301-12/13 some of your typical work assignments may include: The incumbent works under the supervision of the Support Division for the Chief, Mission Assurance Department (a military O-6) and directly coordinates readiness, mandatory, and professional development training for 80 government and military personnel (GS-13 and above and E-7 through O-6) and 220 contract personnel. Develops training related policies and procedures for the department based upon agency and other guidance. Works with the Training and Integration personnel in developing the department's training standard operating procedure. Assists with the development of the quarterly and annual training agenda. Incumbent directly impacts the capabilities, readiness, and professional competence of the Joint Mission Assurance Assessment (JMAA), Balanced Survivability Assessment (BSA), DoD Red teams and Advance Cyber Assessment Tools (ACAT) by ensuring key scientific and technical personnel are trained on the most current and relevant tactics, techniques, and procedures for their area of expertise. In addition, ensures assessment team personnel are capable of world-wide deployment, including hazardous duty areas. Incumbent ensures assessment and mobile training teams are appropriately equipped to accomplish their mission. Independently develops and manages the organization's training and equipment accountability programs. Establishes criteria and schedules to attain training goals and objectives. Explains the Agency and Department's policy and guidelines to new employees. Assists new employees with registration in the Learning Management System (LMS) and schedules personnel for training courses identified as mandatory for agency employees. Establishes a tracking mechanism to ensure all assigned personnel complete required training. Provides quarterly feedback on training records to the supervisors. Processes approved training requests using the established workflow to ensure timelines are met. Monitors the department's training budget and keeps leadership apprised. Coordinates readiness requirements with the Deployment Readiness Cell. Works closely with the Readiness Cell to coordinate training events conducive to the JMAA Schedule. Ensures personnel complete all required training in order to maintain world-wide deployable. Ensures the department's training plans are consistent with the DTRA's Training and Strategic Plans. The incumbent oversees all aspects of the department's equipment management program, including accountability, issue, receipt, research, and maintenance. Through coordination with assigned equipment custodians, defines the baseline equipment issue for each assigned team. Coordinates equipment issue for new personnel through the Acquisition and Logistics. Ensures military members are outfitted with the proper military uniforms with all accoutrements. Plans for and manages systems, subsystems, and equipment throughout their life cycle, including integrated logistics support activities. Develops, initiates, integrates, and manages all logistics actions associated with life cycle management of equipment. Serves as logistics focal point throughout the system's life cycle. Formulates logistics management and fiscal policy for division high value equipment. Analyzes the demand for supplies and forecasts future needs to ensure adequate supplies and equipment are on-hand to support mission needs. Manages the inspection, shipping, handling, and packaging of supplies and equipment to include return of defective equipment for repair. Establishes and monitors warranties on high value items. Evaluates bids and proposals submitted by potential suppliers and recommends the best product that meets the division's needs and is the most cost effective. Maintains accountability for supplies and equipment. Resolves problems related to storage, safety, and other hazards. Manages storage space utilization and develops and maintains a storage facility to include maintenance, future upgrades, and working stock requirements. Schedules and coordinates movement of equipment by commercial or military modes when required. Makes travel arrangements for deploying team members, including military airlift, if required; coordinates passport requirements through coordination with U.S. State Department and Embassies, billeting, ground transportation, country/theatre clearances, and coordinates any assessment-specific requirements. Prepares operations orders/travel authorizations for each deployment of division personnel to conduct assessments or training. The incumbent assumes a leadership role in establishing criterion for the department's mission specialists and enacts policies/procedures to accomplish established objectives. Reviews applicants for mission support specialists' vacancies within the department, provides prioritized selection, conducts interviews.

DLA provides worldwide logistics support for the missions of the Military Departments and the Unified Combatant Commands under conditions of peace and war. It also provides logistics support to other DoD Components and certain Federal agencies, foreign governments, international organizations, and others as authorized.
MajorDuties: If Selected at the GS-0301-13 level, duties will be preformed in a developmental capacity.

Serves as the program manager for Technical and Quality (TQ) Workforce Development, Acquisition Workforce Engineering and Technical Management (ETM) and Test and Evaluation T/E Defense Acquisition Workforce Improvement Act (DAWIA) certifications.

Responsible as the senior advisor to the Technical/Quality Process Owner regarding enterprise-wide TQ functional process performance issues related to training, DLA audits, DLA policy, records management, 508 compliance and related processes.

Serves as lead specialist over TQ processes and systemic issues and problems of particularly high visibility and criticality to the agency.

Conceptualizes in-depth enterprise-wide management studies pertaining to process performance review methodology and procedures to identify problems and develop solutions to improve performance review effectiveness.

Plans, organizes, and directs reviews; assigns segments of the review to various functional process organizations; and coordinates the efforts of the functional analysts/experts throughout the agency.
Coordinate?s findings, provides agency expertise in the development of supplemental guidance for enterprise-wide implementation, and evaluates its impact/effectiveness on TQ functional processes.

Reviews and interprets new or changing policies and procedures, determines their impact on existing/envisioned TQ functions, develops and/or challenges concepts, and provides justification when dealing with precedent setting or problem situations.
Coordinates on behalf of division leadership reporting and internal communications to include TMTs, SITSUMs, and any other specialized request from senior leadership on specific TQ activities.

MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: *** Salary ranges includes local market supplements *** In order to qualify, you must meet the specialized experience requirements described in the Office of Personnel Management (OPM) Qualification Standards for General Schedule Positions, Administrative and Management Positions. This is a GG-13 position in the Defense Civilian Intelligence Personnel System (DCIPS). The GG-13 duties for the "Professional" work category are at the "Full Performance" work level and are equivalent to those at the GS-13 level. The selectee's salary will be set within the grade equivalent to a GS/GG grade based on the selectee's qualifications in relation to the job. SPECIALIZED EXPERIENCE: Your resume must reflect the quality level of experience which demonstrates the possession of the knowledge, skills, abilities, and competencies necessary for successful job performance required for this position. Examples of creditable experience include: knowledge of a wide range of concepts, principles, and practices in a professional or administrative occupation, such as would be gained through extended graduate study or experience and skill in applying this knowledge to difficult and complex work assignments; or a comprehensive, intensive, practical knowledge of a technical field and skill in applying this knowledge to the development of new methods, approaches, or procedures. Incumbent must have a thorough understanding of DoDI 0-3002.05, CJCSM 3500.09, CJCSM 3500.10, DoDM 5200.01 Vl 1-4, Personnel Recovery Security Classification Guide (PR SCG), JP 3-50 and pertinent appendices, and Multi-Service PR and SERE TTPs publications. Note: Creditable experience may include previous military experience, experience gained in the private sector, or experience gained in another government agency. KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS AND ABILITIES (KSAs): Your qualifications will be evaluated on the basis of your level of knowledge, skills, abilities and/or competencies in the following areas: 1. Comprehensive knowledge of DoD PR, SERE, and Code of Conduct policy and guidance, joint doctrine, and joint training and education standards; and SERE training programs to equip at risk DoD personnel to use the Code of Conduct or Principles of Behavior to guide their actions when isolated across the spectrum of military operations and any scenario in the spectrum of captivity possibilities. 2. Extensive knowledge and understanding of the DoD PR functions, DoD PR execution tasks, and DoD PR options, capabilities and methods. 3. Skill in managing operational evasion and recovery training and exercises in austere conditions; managing high- risk role-play activities occurring in a resistance pre academic detention laboratory, resistance academic role-play laboratory; and the resistance training laboratory. 4. Skill in technical writing and mastery of Joint Staff correspondence standards and in verbally communicating critical information to large audiences. 5. Ability to listen and observe academic or laboratory SERE training any hours of the day, for up to 12 consecutive hours in a day, for up to 14 consecutive days; and to listen and observe operational evasion and recovery training occurring outdoors in extreme heat, extreme cold, and uncomfortable conditions for up to 12 consecutive hours in a day, for up to 7-consecutive days. 6. Ability to hike up to 12 hours in a day with a 30 pound pack equipped with essential personal protective SAV documents, while observing operational evasion and recovery experiential training and the evasion and recovery exercise in remote locations. PART-TIME OR UNPAID EXPERIENCE: Credit will be given for appropriate unpaid and or part-time work. You must clearly identify the duties and responsibilities in each position held and the total number of hours per week. VOLUNTEER WORK EXPERIENCE: Refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service Programs (i.e., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community; student and social). Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge and skills that can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment. You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience.

Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: The mission of the United States Air Force is: To fly, fight, and win ... Airpower anytime, anywhere. To achieve that mission, the Air Force has a vision of Global Vigilance, Global Reach and Global Power. That vision orbits around three core competencies: Developing Airmen, Technology-to-Warfighting and Integrating Operations. Core competencies and distinctive capabilities are based on a shared commitment to three core values -- integrity first, service before self, and excellence in all we do. This position is a Defense Civilian Intelligence Personnel Systems (DCIPS) position implemented under Section 504, Title V of Public Law 99-569, Intelligence Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 1987, as codified in Sec 1601, Chap 83 of Title 10 United States Code which sets forth Air Force policies and procedures for DCIPS. This position is in the Excepted Service. MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: To qualify for a Management and Program Analysis Officer, your resume and supporting documentation must support: Specialized Experience: One year of specialized experience that equipped you with the particular competencies to successfully perform the duties of the position, and that is typically in or related to the position to be filled. To qualify at the GS-15 level, applicants must possess one year of specialized experience equivalent to the GS-14 level or equivalent under other pay systems in the Federal service, military or private sector. Applicants must meet eligibility requirements including time-in-grade (General Schedule (GS) positions only), time-after-competitive appointment, minimum qualifications, and any other regulatory requirements by the cut-off/closing date of the announcement. Creditable specialized experience includes: Directing a workforce focused on development of innovative approaches for delivery of HR programs. Analyzing human capital programs to ensure staffing levels, positions, and skills are composed to execute the organization's mission. Leading continuous reviews of mission and program requirements to assess their potential impact on manpower policy. Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community, student, social). Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: America's Combat Logistics Support Agency: The Defense Logistics Agency (DLA) is a U.S. Department of Defense (DoD) agency. DLA provides worldwide logistics support for the missions of the Military Departments and the Unified Combatant Commands under conditions of peace and war. It also provides logistics support to other DoD Components and certain Federal agencies, foreign governments, international organizations, and others as authorized.
MajorDuties: Directs the following assignments in DLA Human Resources: Strategic workforce Planning, Enterprise HR Strategy, Workforce of the Future and its sustainment, Position Management, Manpower Allocations and Authorizations and Organizational Structure.

Analyzes, forecasts, and designs human capital programs and services to ensure that an organization has the right composition of staffing levels, positions, skills, and competencies to execute the organization's mission.
Performs Gap analysis by calculating the difference between workforce demand and workforce supply.
Uses analytical and evaluative methods and techniques to conduct complex program evaluations and oversight of DLA's Human Capital programs.
Responsible for assuring compliance with governing laws and regulations pertaining to use and accountability of civilian authorizations via the Fourth Estate manpower Tracking System (FMTS).
Develops, coordinates, and disseminates policies pertaining to organization structure of the agency.

All applicants tentatively selected for DLA employment in a testing designated position are subject to urinalysis to screen for illegal drug use prior to appointment. Details.JobSummary: About the Position: Serve as a Management Analyst for the Assistant Secretary of the Army (M&RA), Manpower Analysis Agency located at Fort Belvoir, in Fairfax, VA.
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: Civilian employees serve a vital role in supporting the Army mission. They provide the skills that are not readily available in the military, but crucial to support military operations. The Army integrates the talents and skills of its military and civilian members to form a Total Army. The Army values diversity of perspectives, backgrounds, cultures and skills, which connects employees to organizations that are committed to building an inclusive work environment where they can contribute to their fullest potential.
MajorDuties: Conduct manpower and organizational evaluations of all TDA organizations throughout the Army.
Serves as technical expert and team leader in conducting manpower workload and organizational analysis studies.
Develop workload-based staffing standards and performance metrics to determine organizational manning levels.
Recommend changes or improvements in organization, staffing, work methods, and procedures.
Interpret and promulgate policies and doctrinal regulations related to management functions, programs, and methodologies.
